title: The Atlas of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In 1899 Nagasaki, Rosalind Amberdale — half-English, half-Japanese, orphaned daughter of a pearl diver and an indentured clerk — works as a bookkeeper's assistant for the Meridian Trading Company while hiding her mixed parentage behind forged papers. When a census taker notices discrepancies in her household registry, she is blackmailed into helping him audit the company's ledgers, which conceal smuggling, debt bondage, and the sale of indentured divers to a Shanghai syndicate. As the company closes in on the evidence and the harbor workshop where the true ledger is hidden is slated for demolition, Rosalind must rally the found family of dockworkers, divers, and a disgraced interpreter who raised her to finish copying the incriminating pages before the morning tide carries the company's ship — and its proof — out of reach. She finishes the work as the workshop burns, exposes the syndicate through the British consul, and chooses to stay in Nagasaki under her own name rather than sail away as someone else.
about_author: Marguerite Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port records across East Asia before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Salt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Opening on the harbor at dawn: she dives for loose pearls at low tide, then reports to the Meridian Company's counting house. Establishes her double life, her forged papers, and her rule of busy hands and closed mouth. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance.

chapters.title: A Question of Households
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The census taker, Mr. Ishida, visits the tenement and asks about her father's name — one question too many. She lies smoothly, but he writes something down. Emotional beat: first crack in the wall of anonymity.

chapters.title: The Counting House Rules
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her supervisor, Mr. Pell, drills her in the ledgers; she notices columns that don't reconcile — shipments of 'ceramic ware' that weigh like human cargo. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Interpreter's Daughter
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Rosalind's POV. How Kenji Watanabe, a dismissed British-company interpreter, took in the diver's orphaned child and taught her English, figures, and caution. Emotional beat: tenderness and grief for a dead mother.

chapters.title: Ishida Returns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The census taker corners her privately: he knows her mother was Kume, the diver lost off Iojima. He doesn't want money — he wants access to Meridian's shipping manifests. Emotional beat: blackmail dressed as kinship.

chapters.title: The Divers' Landing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She visits the ama divers' beach where her mother once worked and meets old Sato-baasan, who recognizes her face. First hint that divers have been sold north with their debts. Emotional beat: belonging and fear entwined.

chapters.title: Figures That Lie
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working late, she proves the discrepancy: forty-one names entered as crew who never sailed. Pell nearly catches her copying a page. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of knowing.

chapters.title: Kenji's Warning
chapters.summary: Kenji's POV. He reads her copied page and goes pale — he saw this pattern thirty years ago and was ruined for saying so. He orders her to burn it. She hides it instead. Emotional beat: love expressed as fear.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide Schedule
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She learns the syndicate ship Kaiyo-maru sails in three weeks, and that the master ledger lives in the harbor workshop awaiting loading. A deadline forms. Emotional beat: the clock begins.

chapters.title: Sato-baasan's Debt
chapters.summary: Sato-baasan's POV. The old diver reveals her granddaughter is among those sold; her silence was bought with the girl's safety. She gives Rosalind the divers' tally-sticks as corroboration. Emotional beat: guilt transformed into courage.

chapters.title: Pell's Kindness
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Mr. Pell unexpectedly promotes her, raises her pay, and seems genuinely fond of her — making her wonder whether he is complicit or a fellow prisoner. Emotional beat: the ache of liking your possible enemy.

chapters.title: The Workshop at Night
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Ishida's shared POV. They scout the harbor workshop; Ishida confesses his own coercion — the census bureau answers to men above him. Uneasy alliance sealed. Emotional beat: two liars trusting each other anyway.

chapters.title: What the Consul Knows
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She approaches the British consul's clerk under pretense of a passport query and learns the consul will act only on documentary proof, not rumor. Emotional beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Kenji Breaks His Silence
chapters.summary: Kenji's POV. Haunted by the girl he failed to save decades ago, Kenji agrees to translate and authenticate the ledger entries. He teaches Rosalind the old cipher the company uses. Emotional beat: redemption accepted.

chapters.title: The Tally-Sticks Speak
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Matching tally-sticks to ledger lines, she identifies eleven living divers held on the Kaiyo-maru's route. The abstract becomes faces. Emotional beat: resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Pell Closes In
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. He discovers a missing page and suspects his clever little assistant. But he hesitates — we see his own debts to the syndicate and his terror. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as captivity.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ishida offers to register her legally under her mother's name, Kume, erasing the forgery risk but exposing her heritage publicly. She cannot yet decide. Emotional beat: identity as a choice not yet made.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Harbor
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A typhoon halts all loading; the Kaiyo-maru's departure slips days closer to the workshop's demolition date. The found family shelters together in the tenement. Emotional beat: unity forged by weather.

chapters.title: The Copying Begins
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. By lamplight, she, Kenji, and Ishida begin duplicating the master ledger from memory and stolen pages, night after night. Hands cramp; trust deepens. Emotional beat: quiet heroism of ordinary labor.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Tenement
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A neighbor's son, paid in opium, reports the nighttime meetings. Pell now knows everything except where the copies are kept. Emotional beat: paranoia poisoning home.

chapters.title: Sato-baasan Stands Guard
chapters.summary: Sato-baasan's POV. The old diver posts herself outside the copying room and turns away two company men with nothing but her presence and the respect divers command. Emotional beat: fierce grandmotherly defiance.

chapters.title: Halfway Across the Page
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Half the ledger is copied when Pell confronts her gently, offering protection if she stops. She sees his chains and almost pities him — then refuses. Emotional beat: temptation declined.

chapters.title: The Consul's Clerk Wavers
chapters.summary: Ishida's POV. The British clerk warns them the consul may simply hand the matter back to Japanese authorities friendly with Meridian. Proof must be undeniable and public. Emotional beat: the ground shifting beneath them.

chapters.title: Kume's Pearl
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Among her mother's relics she finds a single perfect pearl and a note naming the syndicate's principal — a respected Nagasaki merchant. Grief becomes ammunition. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Official notice: the workshop will be torn down in six days; contents 'disposed of' in three. The deadline collapses. Emotional beat: panic converted to planning.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Ordered to burn the workshop early, Pell stalls, falsifies an inventory, and leaves a key where Rosalind will find it. Emotional beat: a compromised man's small rebellion.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Entries
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The final copying marathon: Rosalind, Kenji, Ishida, and Sato-baasan work until dawn to finish the last third of the ledger. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into devotion.

chapters.title: Fire on the Waterfront
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The syndicate's men torch the workshop ahead of schedule. Rosalind escapes with the completed copy through a burning loading door as the original burns. Emotional beat: survival at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Kenji's POV. Surveying the ruins, Kenji verifies every copied figure against his thirty-year-old memory. The copy is complete and correct. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Ship That Must Not Sail
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Kaiyo-maru will sail on the morning tide with the divers aboard and the syndicate's agent. One night remains to stop it. Emotional beat: desperation crystallizing into action.

chapters.title: Petition at Midnight
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Ishida's POV. They wake the consul with the full copy, the pearl, the note, and Sato-baasan's testimony. The consul, cornered by irrefutable paper, issues a detention order. Emotional beat: the system finally bending.

chapters.title: Harbor Standoff
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At dawn, marines board the Kaiyo-maru as it weighs anchor. The syndicate's agent tears at the ledgers; Pell testifies against his masters. Emotional beat: public reckoning.

chapters.title: Eleven Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On the quay, the detained divers are freed and named one by one; Sato-baasan's granddaughter walks ashore. Rosalind stands among them as kin. Emotional beat: grief answered by reunion.

chapters.title: What Pell Deserves
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Facing charges, Pell names every accomplice but accepts his own sentence. He tells Rosalind she was the best clerk he ever had. Emotional beat: mercy extended without absolution.

chapters.title: The Census Question Again
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ishida brings the corrected registry and asks, formally, what name she wishes entered. She signs 'Amberdale Kume' — both inheritances, no more hiding. Emotional beat: identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The company collapses; the harbor changes hands. Rosalind is offered passage to England and a clean new life. Emotional beat: the seduction of escape.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Standing on the quay as the mail steamer departs, Rosalind watches it go and does not board. Kenji, Sato-baasan, and the divers wait behind her. Emotional beat: home declared.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Her Own
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Epilogue-in-motion: she opens a small accounting office serving divers and dockworkers, keeping honest books for people the trade companies ignored. Emotional beat: purpose rooted.

chapters.title: Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Final chapter: she begins writing this very account, so that the drowned, the sold, and the saved are entered somewhere permanent. Emotional beat: remembrance as victory.

chapters.title: The Atlas Complete
chapters.summary: Closing ensemble coda. One year later: the harbor at dawn, divers singing, the workshop rebuilt as a school, Rosalind teaching children their letters and numbers. The atlas of Nagasaki's harbor is its people. Emotional beat: peace earned.
